meta.paper: Padsumbiya, M., Brahmbhatt, V., Thakkar, S. (2022). Automatic Crack Detection Using Convolutional Neural Network. Journal of Soft Computing in Civil Engineering 6(3). doi:10.22115/SCCE.2022.325596.1397
meta.dataset: Özgenel, Ç.F. (2019), "Concrete Crack Images for Classification", Mendeley Data, V2, doi:10.17632/5y9wdsg2zt.2, CC BY 4.0
meta.architecture: Conv2d(3->128,3x3,valid)+ReLU, MaxPool4, Conv2d(128->128,3x3,valid)+ReLU, MaxPool4, Flatten(6272), Dense(128)+ReLU [L2 0.01 on kernel and bias], Dense(1)+sigmoid
meta.input: 128x128x3 RGB, 227x227 source resized with PIL bilinear, pixel/255
meta.labels: 1 = crack (Positive folder), 0 = no crack (Negative). The paper used the opposite polarity.

split.method: stratified, sklearn train_test_split twice (test 4000, then val 3600), seed 42

hyperparameters.init: Glorot uniform weights, zero biases (Keras defaults)

meta.epoch_log_note: train_acc_running = mean over the epoch while training (as Keras reports); train_acc_end_of_epoch = full training split in eval mode after the epoch; train_seconds excludes evaluation

quantization.rule: int8 symmetric, scale = max|w|/127, q = round(w/scale) clipped to [-127,127]; w = q*scale; per-channel scale indexes the first (output) dimension

layout.fc1: [out][h][w][c] over the 7x7x128 HWC pooled map (flatten index (h*7+w)*128+c)
layout.bin: little-endian, each tensor 4-byte aligned; offset/length in bytes
layout.pytorch_flatten: PyTorch flattens NCHW as (c*7+h)*7+w; fc1 columns were permuted to HWC for export

meta.sample_rule: test images; per class spread evenly over the shipped model's sorted p among correct predictions; the misclassified image with the most confident error is included once; p recomputed from the saved JPEG (q92) re-decoded with PIL
